rationale:
REVISED after Shep's response. Saturday's tempo was 20min at 3:51/km, HR 157, and felt comfortable - exactly as prescribed, not an over-cooked session (the first version misread it because of a bug, now fixed). Sunday's recovery dip was alcohol, not fatigue. Achilles has been zero throughout and he's feeling strong and wants to push on.

So: push the specific things a half marathon needs, not the weekly total. Long run accelerated to 18-20-21km, clearing the 95-minute pre-taper target a week earlier than first proposed and finishing with 21km carrying the last 5km at goal pace - the most race-specific session available. Goal-pace work brought forward to 22 August. Weekly volume deliberately unchanged at a 68km peak: he's a masters athlete seven weeks out with an achilles watch item, and the return on 75km is negative. Goal pace held at 3:54/km for now - the tempo was in super shoes, worth 5-8 sec/km, and one session isn't enough to rewrite it. Revisit on 9 August with two data points.
